# Geometry families 348–361: scoped result

Two manuscripts fully read at release commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`: family 356's weak-Hessian companion (11 pages) and family 357's coordinate construction (43 pages). All fourteen assigned families read at overview depth. The main Gigli-characterization manuscript was only excerpt-read through page 9.

The strongest reusable candidates are:

1. **Weak Hessian -> every geodesic:** bounded Lipschitz drift reweighting, resolvent regularity for weighted multipliers, and closure in the common generator graph domain. This repairs the weighted test-class obstruction identified by Brena–Gigli. The exact core calculation and entropy localization were reconstructed. The family Lean label covers this companion, not the whole curvature characterization; transitive formal proof checking was not performed.
2. **Directional energy -> open charts:** the value-space update `h_{i+1}=h_i+(Dh_i)^{-T}v_i` converts positive covector derivatives into pullback-metric increments. A diagonal second-jet recurrence and an all-order Gevrey majorant keep metric errors summable even with divergent/noncommuting inverse Gram forms and divergent `sum sqrt(E_i)`. The finite-dimensional algebra and final all-pairs argument were checked internally. The decisive geometric input remains the sharp two-center directional estimate, Proposition 4.10, followed by the simultaneous bootstrap, Proposition 5.4.

Three substantive deductions/constructions are in [TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](</Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/Literature Digestion/notes/frontier_geometry2/cycle19/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md>): a finite-parameter geodesic chord bound that charges entropy, endpoint-routing continuity, and drift conditioning; an exact harmonic-cone obstruction showing finite smooth corrections can converge uniformly to a bi-Lipschitz limit while every finite correction fails the all-scale lower distance bound; and conditional local Lipschitz contractions/current fillings with constant `L^(2k+2)/(k+1)` near every regular point.

The cone proof is analytic. [CONE_CHECK.json](</Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/Literature Digestion/results/frontier_geometry2/cycle19/CONE_CHECK.json>) records a reproducible finite arithmetic check of nine smoothing cases and the limiting metric bounds. Run `python3 work/frontier_geometry2/cycle19/cone_finite_stage.py` from the workspace. Fi
